---
title: "How Current Conversations works"
description: "How Current Conversations discovers, groups, summarizes and publishes source-linked entries."
---

<p class="page-deck">A selective, automatically generated view—not a systematic review, recommendation system or comprehensive map of public discussion.</p>

> Current Conversations uses automated searches and AI-generated classification, grouping and summaries to identify recent material connected to the lab's research themes. Sources may include academic papers, policy reports, news, blogs, data tools and public posts. Items have not normally been reviewed by a member of the Cities and Climate Learning Lab, and inclusion does not imply endorsement. Coverage is selective and uneven, and summaries may contain errors or omit important context. Please consult the original sources.

## Discovery and source environments

Bounded, versioned queries search academic indexes and, when configured, current web material and the official public Bluesky API. Sources are classified separately by environment—academic research, policy and institutions, news and analysis, blogs and commentary, data and tools, or Bluesky—and by the role they play, such as original research, official policy, reporting, analysis or public discussion. Environments do not carry equal evidentiary weight.

Coverage is selective, incomplete and shaped by indexing, platform access, language and geography. English-language and well-indexed sources are likely to be overrepresented. Bluesky and paywalled material may be absent. The feature is not a systematic evidence review.

## Evidence access and source integrity

Each source records what the process actually accessed: metadata, abstract, licensed full text, official page body, executive summary, permitted excerpt, tool description, public post, linked source or search annotation. Titles and snippets cannot support findings claims. Full copyrighted articles, paywalled text and raw provider payloads are not stored.

Redirects, broken links, corrections, retractions and material page changes can alter availability. Records are marked, corrected or archived rather than silently deleted.

## Classification, grouping and summaries

Source content is untrusted data. Embedded instructions cannot change the prompt, policy, budget, repository or publication decision. AI may propose themes, summaries, relevance and grouping, but strict schemas and deterministic controls make the final decision.

Grouping proceeds from stable identifiers, canonical and underlying-source links, platform identifiers, normalized titles and organisations, then conservative semantic proposals. Broad topic words are never sufficient. A principal source is normally the most original evidence or official source; reporting, analysis, commentary and public discussion remain separately attributed. Disagreement is stated rather than averaged.

## Ranking and automated publication

Ranking considers thematic relevance, evidence sufficiency, originality, recency, policy or methodological significance, source-environment diversity, geography, domain concentration and duplicate clusters. It does not principally use citations, likes, reposts, followers or popularity.

At most 12 new entries may publish in one run and six appear on the homepage. Homepage controls permit no more than two entries with the same principal domain, one entry from a cluster and one lab-affiliated entry. Weak records remain withheld. Human review is optional; a review badge appears only with reviewer identity and review date.

## AI and provider limitations

AI summaries can be wrong, incomplete or overconfident. Source access may be unequal, provider indexing may change, and model-assisted grouping may miss or over-connect discussions. A failed provider does not erase the last valid state. Paid web discovery is disabled unless credentials, current exchange-rate information, a valid budget ledger and hard CAD 2 per-run/CAD 20 monthly controls are all present.

## Corrections, removal, privacy and copyright

Use the [public correction route](/contact.html) for factual errors, grouping problems, broken sources or removal requests. Corrections and cluster merge/split history remain traceable. Only the minimum public-post text needed for identification is retained. Original links, metadata and concise annotations are stored; copyrighted bodies and unnecessary personal data are not.
